caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 1059 of 2004
lawyer:
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md SR Khoshnabish, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Ozair Farooq, Senior Advocate, (Abul Kalam Mainuddin, Advocate with him) instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For Respondent Nos. 1-3, 5-16. 
Not represented—Respondent Nos. 4, 17-37.
parties:
Anwarul Azim and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Fatema Khatoon and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated February 25, 2004 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 86 of 2002 dismissing the same. The appeal was filed against the judgment and decree dated January 23, 2002 of the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 13 of 1993 decreeing the same. The suit was filed seeking saham of 6.93 acres of land on partition of the land in suit and for a declaration that the deed of gift dated August 25, 1984 in favour of the defendant No. 1 was forged and fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 6. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record arrived at the finding that the deed of gift dated August 25, 1984 was a fraudulent one and by the said deed defendant No. 1 did not acquire any title. The trial Court also did not accept the defendant No. 1's case of oral gift by defendant No. 25 and Gulbahar, predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4. The trial Court rejected the plaintiffs' claim as regard the shares of Bangladesh Oxygen Limited. The trial Court decreed the suit allotting saham of 6.65 acres of land out of the land described in schedule 'Ka', 'Kha', 'Ga' and 'Gha'. 

 8. The learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the High Court Division was in error in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court without considering the evidence on record as regard discharging the special onus of the defendant No. 1, that the High Court Division was in error in not considering the evidence as to the last desire of Saleh (owner of the land) to make gift of his land to the defendant No. 1 and that also disclosure of such desire to the donors and others, that the High Court Division was in error in not considering the fact that two of the donors filed written statement supporting the case of the defendant No. 1, that the High Court Division was in error in holding that it was not proved that there was offer and acceptance and delivery of possession, that the finding of the High Court Division that the deed of gift is forged and fraudulent is not sustainable in law. 

 9. The submissions so made merit no consideration since the High Court Division as well as the trial Court upon detailed discussions of the evidence of the parties concurrently held that the deed of gift was a fraudulent one. It is seen from the evidence on record that the defendant No.1 obtained the signature of the donors on misrepresentation, in that the donee represented to the donors that their signatures are being obtained for withdrawing money from the bank. There was no independent witness to support the defendant's case that Saleh during his lifetime expressed his desire to give his property to the defendant No.1 and that if, because of illness, he cannot complete the execution and registration of deed of gift the donors would complete the deed. The undenied position is that the donors were illiterate pardanishin village women and the defendant No. 1 in succession certificate case acted as Tadbirkar of the said women i.e. donors. The concurrent finding is that no evidence was led from the side of the defendant No. 1 that the donors executed the document in question i.e. deed of gift, having had independent advice about the transaction and being aware of the nature of transaction and the contents of the document. In the facts and circumstances of the case, the burden was on the defendant No. 1 to establish that the donors executed the documents having had independent advice and also having had the knowledge about the transaction and the contents of the document. The defendant No. 1 miserably failed to establish the said fact and, in that state of the matter, the suit having been decreed by the trial Court and the same having been affirmed by the High Court Division we are of the view no interference is called for with the judgment and decree sought to be appealed. It has been submitted that two of the donors submitted written statement supporting the defendant No. 1. The said two defendants or any one of them ultimately, did not depose in the Court in support of their case as was in their written statement and, as such, the written statement so filed was of no purpose to the defendant No. 1.
